passage.text: Every day, some callers will be angry.
passage.reading: ˈɛvri ˈdeɪ, sʌm ˈkɔːlərz wɪl bi ˈæŋɡri.

passage.text: Remember: they are angry about the problem, not about you.
passage.reading: rɪˈmɛmbər: ðeɪ ər ˈæŋɡri əˈbaʊt ðə ˈprɑːbləm, ˈnɑːt əˈbaʊt juː.

passage.text: Listen first, and let the caller explain the problem.
passage.reading: ˈlɪsən ˈfɜːrst, ənd ˈlɛt ðə ˈkɔːlər ɪkˈspleɪn ðə ˈprɑːbləm.

passage.text: Speak slowly and calmly, even if the caller is shouting.
passage.reading: ˈspiːk ˈsloʊli ənd ˈkɑːmli, ˈiːvən ɪf ðə ˈkɔːlər ɪz ˈʃaʊtɪŋ.

passage.text: Apologize, and show that you understand.
passage.reading: əˈpɑːlədʒaɪz, ənd ˈʃoʊ ðæt juː ˌʌndərˈstænd.

passage.text: Your script gives you useful sentences, such as "I'm sorry you've had this problem."
passage.reading: jʊr ˈskrɪpt ˈɡɪvz juː ˈjuːsfəl ˈsɛntənsɪz, ˈsʌtʃ əz aɪm ˈsɑːri juːv ˈhæd ðɪs ˈprɑːbləm.

passage.text: But don't just read the script. Speak like a real person.
passage.reading: bʌt ˈdoʊnt ˈdʒʌst ˈriːd ðə ˈskrɪpt. ˈspiːk ˈlaɪk ə ˈriːəl ˈpɜːrsən.

passage.text: If a caller is rude, warn them politely once.
passage.reading: ɪf ə ˈkɔːlər ɪz ˈruːd, ˈwɔːrn ðɛm pəˈlaɪtli ˈwʌns.

passage.text: If they don't stop, transfer the call to your supervisor.
passage.reading: ɪf ðeɪ ˈdoʊnt ˈstɑːp, trænsˈfɜːr ðə ˈkɔːl tə jʊr ˈsuːpərvaɪzər.

passage.text: Never promise something that you can't do.
passage.reading: ˈnɛvər ˈprɑːmɪs ˈsʌmθɪŋ ðæt juː ˈkænt ˈduː.

passage.text: Keep a record of every call: the caller's name, the problem and what you promised.
passage.reading: ˈkiːp ə ˈrɛkərd əv ˈɛvri ˈkɔːl: ðə ˈkɔːlərz ˈneɪm, ðə ˈprɑːbləm ənd ˈwʌt juː ˈprɑːmɪst.

passage.text: This helps your colleagues if the customer calls again.
passage.reading: ðɪs ˈhɛlps jʊr ˈkɑːliːɡz ɪf ðə ˈkʌstəmər ˈkɔːlz əˈɡɛn.

passage.text: Thank you for your patience. You are the voice of our company!
passage.reading: ˈθæŋk juː fər jʊr ˈpeɪʃəns. juː ər ðə ˈvɔɪs əv aʊr ˈkʌmpəni!
